Sam's own words for points 7a, 7b, 8, 8a and 9 sit in the quote at lines 84-109; claims 43 and 60 are Sam's rulings, claims 44-59 are the orchestrator's application of his principles. Claims below follow the file's order: Sam's quoted decisions first, then each listed claim split into one fact per claim, with gaps where the ruling leaves something open.

claims.statement: The overview, check your answers, declaration and confirmation pages are each owned by an individual journey set.

claims.statement: Changes made to the live-animals overview, check your answers, declaration and confirmation pages are also made to the plants equivalents, so the two are consistent as a starting point.
claims.quote: That doesn't mean we only want to apply this to live animals. Make these consistent as a starting point. [In plants] as well.

claims.statement: Set ownership of these pages is kept so that each set may have differing designs later if that becomes required, but consistency comes first.
claims.quote: It just enables us to have differing designs if that becomes required, but step one should be consistency.

claims.statement: When a change is implemented on animals, the matching plants page is changed to match it.
claims.quote: If you're implementing changes here to animals, match it up on plants.

claims.statement: The backlog does not add a separate plants increment for each animals increment to check for a plants equivalent.
claims.quote: it's massive overkill to double the number of increments to see if there's an [plants] equivalent.

claims.statement: A workflow step identifies the pages and behaviour animals and plants have in common, and where a change is required in both.
claims.quote: A workflow: go through and identify common pages, common behaviour, and where it's required.
claims.note: The plants-common-mapping-2026-10-09.json evidence file is the orchestrator's run of this step (preamble lines 132-133).

claims.statement: Plants and animals get a common change at the same time, in the same increment, because adding an increment is relatively expensive.
claims.quote: [Plants] and animals get that change at the same time. The overhead of adding an increment is relatively expensive, so we don't want to be needlessly separating things.

claims.statement: Changing the animals dashboard so it looks more like the prototype's animals dashboard is wanted, possibly as a separate theme.
claims.quote: Something we could potentially do, maybe as a separate theme, is changes to the animals dashboard, so the animals dashboard looks more like the animals dashboard on the prototype. That'd be good.
claims.note: Answers point 8 of answers-2026-10-09-pm.md; ruled on in full in ruling:sam-2026-10-09-templates.
